title: Explore programs
description: Find programs that fit what you want to study, how you want to learn, and when you want to start. Save the ones you like to compare them.

title: Request information
description: Tell us what interests you, and an admissions counselor will send details about programs, costs, and next steps.

title: Request information
description: Tell us which programs interest you, and a graduate admissions advisor will send details about requirements, funding, and next steps.

title: Visit campus
description: Take a tour, sit in on a class, and talk with an admissions counselor. Online sessions work if you can't come in person.

title: Apply
description: Submit your application by your program's deadline. It's free for Washington residents and takes about 30 minutes.

title: Apply, with transcripts and recommendations
description: Submit your application by your program's deadline, with transcripts from every college you've attended and two letters of recommendation.

title: Send transcripts from every college you've attended
description: Ask each college to send an official transcript. Unofficial copies are fine while we review your application.

title: Send English proficiency scores
description: Send TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores, unless English is your first language or you studied in English.

title: Submit your FAFSA or WASFA
description: File by the priority date to be considered for the most grants and scholarships. Use the WASFA if you can't file the FAFSA. File again every year.

title: Send financial documents for your I-20
description: Show that you can cover a year of tuition and living costs. We need these before we can issue your I-20.

title: Apply for housing
description: First-year students get priority for the residence halls. Apply early for the best choice of rooms.

title: Ask about assistantships
description: Teaching and research assistantships cover tuition and pay a stipend. Ask your program about openings when you apply.

title: Get your credits evaluated
description: After you're admitted, the Transfer Center shows how your credits apply to your program, so you know what's left.

title: Plan your schedule with an advisor
description: Build a schedule that fits around work and family, with evening, hybrid, and online classes, and ask about credit for prior learning.

title: Confirm your place
description: Pay the $200 enrollment deposit to hold your place. It's credited to your first tuition bill.

title: Accept your offer of admission
description: Accept your offer and pay the enrollment deposit to hold your place in your program.

title: Get your I-20 and apply for a visa
description: When your I-20 arrives, pay the SEVIS fee and book your F-1 visa interview. Interview waits can take several weeks.

title: Attend first-year orientation
description: Meet your advisor, register for your first classes, and get your student ID. Families are welcome on the first morning.

title: Attend transfer orientation
description: Meet your advisor, review how your credits apply, and register for your first classes.

title: Attend graduate orientation
description: Meet your program director and other new graduate students, and learn about funding, research support, and campus resources.

title: Meet with your advisor
description: Check your degree progress and plan next term's classes before registration opens.

title: Register for classes
description: Sign up as soon as registration opens for the best choice of sections.

title: Pay tuition
description: Pay your bill or set up a payment plan with Student Accounts by the due date to keep your classes.

title: Finalize your schedule
description: Add or drop classes by the deadline. After that, changes need an instructor's approval.
